title: Bedrock Spend Controls threat model
asset: The Bedrock bill, bounded per identity, tenant, or workload; correct usage attribution; enforcement within the documented bound (metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation)); authorized and audited administration. Prompt confidentiality is out of scope: the broker never sees inference traffic and payload delivery is disabled.

status_legend.Mitigated: A control exists in code and is covered by tests.
status_legend.Accepted: Known residual risk, documented, not planned.
status_legend.Open: No control; listed so it is not forgotten.

boundaries.name: Broker -> STS / IAM
boundaries.crosses: AssumeRole with RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity = sanitized claim; inline session policy

boundaries.name: Vended session -> Bedrock
boundaries.crosses: IAM authorization of bedrock:InvokeModel*/CountTokens on allowed_model_arns; invocation log is the metering truth

boundaries.name: Invocation logs -> usage processor -> DynamoDB
boundaries.crosses: CloudWatch Logs subscription; identity.arn and modelId; transactional ledger writes

boundaries.name: DynamoDB streams -> enforcement processors -> IAM policy versions
boundaries.crosses: REVOCATION# sentinels, CONFIG#EMERGENCY_STOP; CreatePolicyVersion on pre-attached policies; PutRolePolicy on workload roles

boundaries.crosses: Shared admin key or admin JWT claim; separate break-glass key; If-Match + Idempotency-Key

boundaries.name: Operator / account administrator -> out-of-band IAM, SCP, logging

assets.name: Bedrock spend
assets.description: The account's Bedrock bill, bounded per user identity, tenant, or workload. The primary asset: every other asset matters because it protects this one.

assets.name: vended credentials
assets.description: Short-lived STS sessions for BedrockUserRole carrying RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity = the sanitized identity claim and a lease-deadline session policy.

assets.name: usage ledger
assets.description: Usage table: canonical daily rows, per-model rows, RATE# minute counters, REQUEST# idempotency markers, and stored RECONCILE# runs.

assets.name: quota configuration and subject status
assets.description: Users table: limits, thresholds, model budgets, status and status_origin, logical leases, SESSION# maps, REVOCATION# sentinels, CONFIG# control rows.

assets.name: administrative secrets
assets.description: Routine admin key and break-glass emergency key in Secrets Manager; the admin JWT claim/value configuration that gates the console.

assets.name: enforcement IAM policies
assets.description: Per-user SourceIdentity deny shards, emergency deny policy versions, workload inline denies, the permissions boundary, and BedrockUserRole itself.

assets.name: administrative audit trail
assets.description: Admin audit table events and idempotency records; CONFIG#ENFORCEMENT_AUDIT# and EMERGENCY_AUDIT# rows.

assets.name: metering source
assets.description: Bedrock model invocation logging configuration, the managed log group, and the CloudWatch Logs subscription to the usage processor.

assets.name: price catalog and workload roster
assets.description: The reviewed price catalog and per-model overrides (configuration.py), the SSM price snapshot, and the SSM workload roster the console reads.

assets.name: account cost data
assets.description: Aggregate Bedrock cost for the Region read from Cost Explorer by the opt-in reconciliation Lambda and stored as RECONCILE# rows.

out_of_scope_assets: Prompts and completions: the broker never sees inference traffic and the logging configuration disables payload delivery, so their confidentiality is not a property this sample can affect.

assumptions.content: The identity provider is trusted and the attribute configured as jwt_user_claim is stable and not editable by the end user (the default sub is safe). Group membership behind admin_jwt_claim is managed by the IdP administrators.

Account administrators (IAM, SCP, Bedrock logging configuration, DynamoDB console) are trusted. The sample cannot constrain the account's management plane; production applies the SCP or DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and relies on CloudTrail for administrator accountability.

Model invocation logging is the metering truth: identity.arn, modelId, requestId, and token counts are populated by the Bedrock service and cannot be forged by the caller. requestMetadata is caller-controlled and is never used for attribution.

Model invocation logging does not capture StartAsyncInvoke, InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, or anything on the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Operators who need strict accounting exclude models used through those APIs from allowed_model_arns and deny bedrock-mantle:* alongside bedrock:*.

End users reach Bedrock only through vended credentials; workload-mode applications call Bedrock with their own IAM role attributed by an application inference profile. No other principal in the account retains bedrock:InvokeModel* (production enforces this with an SCP).

Overspend is bounded, not zero. The design guarantee is metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation); real-time cut-off is not a goal, and the bound must be measured in the deploying account (see qualification/QUALIFICATION.md).

Production restricts invoker_principal_arns so that only the application backends can call the broker Function URL; the broker is never exposed to anonymous callers, and token theft alone is insufficient to vend.

The routine admin key and the break-glass key are held by operators, rotated per the gateway runbook, and never reach a browser: the console authorizes by admin JWT group and SigV4, and the break-glass key is typed per action.

The reviewed price catalog and its overrides change only through Git review; the SSM price snapshot and workload roster are written only by CloudFormation, so a wrong price is a review failure rather than a runtime attack.

Reconciliation is opt-in. When enabled it reads Cost Explorer for the settled day (reconcile_lag_days) and the cost-allocation tag has been activated at the payer account; Cost Explorer data is account-wide by nature.
This is educational sample code, not a managed service: an adopter runs their own security review and adapts invoker_principal_arns, allowed_model_arns, the SCP, and alerting before production use.

A SESSION# map row cannot be needed after the STS credential it describes has expired (at most 3 600 s), so a usage_retention_days TTL with a 31-day floor only loses attribution for records delivered days late.

grammar.prerequisites: who has captured a valid user JWT before its expiry and also holds an IAM principal allowed on the broker Function URL
grammar.threat_action: present the captured token to the broker
grammar.threat_impact: credentials vended under the victim's identity and spend charged to the victim's quota until the token expires

threats.title: JWT forgery or replay
threats.description: Attacker presents a fabricated or captured token to obtain credentials under another identity.
threats.mitigation: Signature verified against issuer JWKS (RS/ES) or dev-only HS256; iss/aud/exp enforced, and only the first configured audience is accepted on /v1/credentials (a console-client token cannot vend); discovery and JWKS must be HTTPS; lease deadline capped at token exp so a replayed token cannot mint credentials that outlive it. The client library keys its per-user cache on a claim read without signature verification, so it requires the application to verify the token first (verified_identity= / client_for_identity reject a mismatch).
threats.residual_risk: A token stolen before exp is usable until then; no jti replay cache. Caller must also hold a SigV4 principal allowed on the Function URL.

grammar.prerequisites: whose IdP lets them edit the attribute configured as jwt_user_claim (for example a self-service preferred_username)
grammar.threat_action: set their quota identity claim to another subject's value
grammar.threat_impact: spend accounted to and blocks applied against the wrong subject

threats.title: jwt_user_claim user-controlled or IdP misconfigured
threats.description: If the quota claim is user-editable at the IdP, one user can spend another's budget.
threats.mitigation: Reserved prefixes and the workload: namespace are rejected; documentation directs operators to a stable IdP-controlled claim (default sub).
threats.residual_risk: IdP configuration is outside the sample.

grammar.prerequisites: with a valid JWT and an allowed SigV4 principal
grammar.threat_action: request credentials in a tight loop
grammar.threat_impact: STS AssumeRole throttling and DynamoDB write pressure that starve other users' vends

threats.title: Vend flooding
threats.description: A client refreshes credentials in a loop, exhausting STS or DynamoDB.
threats.mitigation: Per-identity vend rate limit (VEND#<user>#<minute>, vend_rate_limit_per_minute) -> 429, summed across processes; one logical lease per identity: a new lease ID before refresh_after joins the current lease without extending its deadline; Function URL requires a SigV4 principal from invoker_principal_arns.
threats.residual_risk: Many valid identities multiply the per-identity budget; SigV4 scopes who can try.

grammar.prerequisites: holding a vend response
grammar.threat_action: read another subject's limits or usage from the quota response headers
grammar.threat_impact: disclosure of a third party's budget and consumption

threats.title: Quota headers leak another user's state
threats.description: Response headers could expose limits of other subjects.
threats.mitigation: Headers describe only the authenticated identity's own limits.

grammar.prerequisites: who can choose or influence an identity claim that sanitizes to another subject's RoleSessionName
grammar.threat_action: obtain a session whose SourceIdentity maps to a different subject
grammar.threat_impact: usage credited to the wrong ledger row and revocation denies matching the wrong sessions

threats.title: Session-name collision or injection
threats.description: Two identities sanitize to the same RoleSessionName, or a crafted claim escapes the session-name character set, so metering or revocation targets the wrong subject.
threats.mitigation: session_name_for derives a collision-resistant name (sanitized prefix + hash of the full claim) and the same value is SourceIdentity; the exact stamped value is persisted on the user row (source_identity) so revocation never re-derives it; SESSION# reverse map; SetSourceIdentity/TagSession granted only to the broker role on the trust policy; the role's trust policy requires sts:SourceIdentity (Null=false), so no BedrockUserRole session can exist without a stamped identity.

grammar.prerequisites: whose lease session policy carries Resource "*"
grammar.threat_action: invoke a model that is not in allowed_model_arns
grammar.threat_impact: unmetered or unpriced spend on models the operator never approved

threats.title: Session policy widens access
threats.description: The Resource:"*" in the lease session policy could grant models outside the allowlist.
threats.mitigation: STS intersects the session policy with the role policy and the permissions boundary; "*" only applies the DateLessThan deadline to the existing allowlist. Role grants exactly CountTokens, InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream. Both the role policy and the boundary carry an explicit Deny on application-inference-profile/* and provisioned-model/* and on StartAsyncInvoke / InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, so even allowed_model_arns ["*"] cannot reach a workload profile, provisioned throughput, or an unmetered invoke path.

grammar.prerequisites: if bedrock:CallWithBearerToken were ever granted to the vended role
grammar.threat_action: mint a Bedrock API key and call any model with it
grammar.threat_impact: defeat of the per-model ARN allowlist and of metering attribution

threats.title: Bearer-token bypass of the model allowlist
threats.description: bedrock:CallWithBearerToken requires Resource:"*" and would defeat the per-model ARN allowlist.
threats.mitigation: Not granted on the vended role, boundary, or session policy; DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and the SCP example explicitly deny it for other principals.

grammar.prerequisites: holding bedrock-mantle:CreateInference or bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken (a vended session never does; it is denied by omission)
grammar.threat_action: run inference through the bedrock-mantle endpoint
grammar.threat_impact: spend that model-invocation logging never records

threats.title: bedrock-mantle endpoint bypass
threats.description: bedrock-mantle:CreateInference / CallWithBearerToken is a separate IAM service prefix and Bedrock Mantle calls are not captured by model-invocation logging; if reachable, spend is invisible to metering.
threats.mitigation: The vended role's identity policy, the permissions boundary, and the session policy grant only bedrock:* actions, so a vended session has no bedrock-mantle:* permission (denied by omission) and the boundary prevents adding it by editing the role alone.
threats.residual_risk: Other principals in the account with bedrock-mantle:* spend unmetered; DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and the SCP example should be extended with bedrock-mantle:CreateInference and bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken where Mantle is not wanted. Documented in README 'Metering coverage caveat'.
threats.status_detail: Mitigated for vended sessions; Accepted (documented) for other principals

grammar.prerequisites: with vended credentials
grammar.threat_action: populate requestMetadata with another subject's identifier
grammar.threat_impact: misattributed usage if the metadata were trusted for accounting

threats.title: requestMetadata spoofing
threats.description: The caller controls requestMetadata in the invocation log.
threats.mitigation: Never read for attribution; only identity.arn (Bedrock-populated) and modelId are used.

grammar.prerequisites: whose allowed_model_arns includes a model reachable through StartAsyncInvoke or InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream
grammar.threat_action: generate video, images, or speech through those APIs
grammar.threat_impact: spend that produces no invocation-log record and never reaches the ledger

threats.title: Unmetered Runtime APIs
threats.description: StartAsyncInvoke and InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream authorize under bedrock:InvokeModel* but produce no invocation-log record.
threats.mitigation: The vended role policy and its permissions boundary explicitly Deny bedrock:StartAsyncInvoke and bedrock:InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, so a vended session cannot use the two Runtime paths that model-invocation logging does not record, whatever allowed_model_arns says. The SCP example denies the same actions for other principals.
threats.residual_risk: Other principals in the account that hold these actions (and bedrock-mantle:*) still spend unmetered unless the SCP is applied; see T-26. Reconciliation shows the gap as a positive delta.

grammar.prerequisites: calling an image model while imageDataDeliveryEnabled is false on the logging configuration
grammar.threat_action: generate images whose log record carries neither token counts nor a body
grammar.threat_impact: requests counted but priced at $0 with no unpriced-dimension flag to alarm on

threats.title: Image generation priced at zero when image delivery is off
threats.description: A Nova Canvas record with imageDataDeliveryEnabled=false carries no token counts and no body, so images=0 and cost $0 with no missing_dimensions flag.
threats.mitigation: The record is still counted as a request (image-model heuristic prevents it being skipped as metadata-less) so volume is visible; README tells operators to enable image delivery or exclude image models.
threats.residual_risk: The one pricing gap the fallback alarm cannot detect.

grammar.prerequisites: with logs:DeleteLogGroup or bedrock:PutModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration
grammar.threat_action: disable, redirect, or delete the invocation log
grammar.threat_impact: metering going blind while spend continues

threats.title: Invocation-log tampering or deletion by an account administrator
threats.description: logs:DeleteLogGroup or PutModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration removes or redirects the metering source.
threats.mitigation: Managed log group and logging configuration are RemovalPolicy.RETAIN; writer role trust is condition-scoped to aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn. Opt-in reconciliation (reconciliation_enabled) is the detection control.
threats.residual_risk: An administrator can turn logging off; only detectable after the fact.

grammar.prerequisites: already at a block threshold while log delivery or stream processing is delayed
grammar.threat_action: keep invoking models during the detection window
grammar.threat_impact: spend above the budget up to metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation)

threats.title: Metering lag or stream lag leading to overspend
threats.description: Slow log delivery or a backed-up subscription delays detection.
threats.mitigation: Overspend bounded by construction: metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation); lease deadline embedded in the credential and non-extending on retry; DetectionLagMilliseconds measured per record.
threats.residual_risk: The bound must be measured in the deploying account (qualification/QUALIFICATION.md); workload mode has no lease (T-19).

grammar.prerequisites: when the CloudWatch Logs subscription retries a batch that was already applied
grammar.threat_action: apply the same invocation record twice or lose an increment
grammar.threat_impact: inflated usage that blocks a subject early, or usage that is never charged

threats.title: Double-charging or lost increments on retry
threats.description: CloudWatch Logs delivery is at-least-once.
threats.mitigation: One TransactWriteItems with a conditional REQUEST#<id> marker Put plus subject and per-model ledger Updates; a cancelled transaction re-reads the marker before classifying as duplicate.

grammar.prerequisites: arriving after its SESSION# map row has expired (TTL usage_retention_days, floor 31 days)
grammar.threat_action: reach the processor without a resolvable subject
grammar.threat_impact: usage that is logged as unresolved and never charged to anyone

threats.title: Unresolved session -> usage silently lost
threats.description: A SESSION# map row expired so a late record cannot be attributed.
threats.mitigation: Logged as unresolved_sessions warning; retention floor 31 days; a session cannot outlive the vended STS credential (<= 3600 s).
threats.residual_risk: Only for records delivered days late.

grammar.prerequisites: holding live vended credentials in the seconds after CreatePolicyVersion succeeds
grammar.threat_action: keep invoking models until the deny propagates
grammar.threat_impact: spend inside the documented propagation window

threats.title: IAM eventual consistency
threats.description: CreatePolicyVersion succeeds but takes seconds to propagate; sessions keep working meanwhile.
threats.mitigation: Propagation is inside the documented bound; the lease is the fallback.
threats.residual_risk: Seconds of continued access after a block.

grammar.prerequisites: able to drive many subjects over quota so that their SourceIdentity values land in one 6 144-character deny shard
grammar.threat_action: fill the shard past the IAM policy size limit
grammar.threat_impact: new identities hashed to that shard not being IAM-cut (the lease bound still applies)

threats.title: Revocation shard overflow
threats.description: Blocking many identities fills a 6144-character shard; new identities in that shard are not IAM-cut.
threats.mitigation: Processor keeps the last-good deny set rather than clearing it; RevocationPolicyOverflowAlarm; lease still bounds new identities; shard count immutable to prevent rehash gaps. The nightly auto-block sweep (T-31) evicts identities whose automatic block is already stale, so shard capacity is consumed only by currently over-quota subjects.
threats.residual_risk: Capacity ~800-1100 simultaneously blocked identities; beyond that, new blocks rely on the lease.

grammar.prerequisites: executing with the revocation, emergency, or workload-enforcer role
grammar.threat_action: use its IAM permissions to attach or author policies beyond its designated targets
grammar.threat_impact: the vended role or another principal gaining permissions the operator never approved

threats.title: Enforcement processors escalate via IAM
threats.description: A compromised processor uses its IAM permissions to grant itself or the vended role wider access.
threats.mitigation: Revocation and emergency processors may only version their designated pre-attached policy ARNs (no AttachRolePolicy/CreatePolicy/role edits); the vended role's permissions boundary caps any policy version; workload enforcer PutRolePolicy scoped to exact configured role ARNs; emergency processor DynamoDB access restricted with dynamodb:LeadingKeys.

grammar.prerequisites: when PutRolePolicy on its role fails or is delayed
grammar.threat_action: keep calling Bedrock with its own long-lived IAM credentials
grammar.threat_impact: unbounded spend until the inline deny lands, because workload mode has no lease fallback

threats.title: Workload enforcement failure has no lease fallback
threats.description: A blocked workload keeps spending until PutRolePolicy succeeds; workload mode has no vend path and therefore no permission lease.
threats.mitigation: WorkloadEnforcementFailureAlarm; 5-minute repair schedule; manual attach procedure in the runbook.
threats.residual_risk: The only unbounded-overspend path in the system; alarmed.

grammar.prerequisites: adding a third consumer to the users-table stream
grammar.threat_action: throttle the two enforcement readers
grammar.threat_impact: delayed revocation and emergency-stop propagation

threats.title: Stream consumer starvation
threats.description: A third users-table stream consumer would throttle the two enforcement readers.
threats.mitigation: Dispatcher fan-out design; synth test asserts exactly two EventSourceMappings.

grammar.prerequisites: running with a defective criterion, a stale read, or under an attacker's control
grammar.threat_action: write active to a blocked row that should have held
grammar.threat_impact: an over-quota or admin-frozen subject regaining credentials without a human decision

threats.title: Nightly sweep lifts a block that should have held
threats.description: AutoBlockSweeperFn writes active to blocked user rows on a schedule without a human in the loop. A bug in its criterion, a stale read, or a compromised function would unblock subjects still over quota, or unblock an admin freeze.
threats.mitigation: Criterion is the broker's own (row_enforcement.over_budget in the shared layer, also exercised by the workload-enforcer suite); only automatic-origin rows are candidates and status_origin admin is never written; each lift is a TransactWriteItems conditional on observed version/status/status_reason so a concurrent admin block or re-block wins and the sweep counts a race; the REVOCATION# sentinel rides in the same transaction so row and deny shards cannot disagree; no iam:* permissions; a wrongly lifted subject is re-blocked at its next vend or metered request through the existing paths.
threats.residual_risk: A failed pass leaves stale automatic blocks: availability for those users and slow shard growth, never under-enforcement; visible for a day via AutoBlockSweepFailureAlarm and the console card.

grammar.prerequisites: who obtains the routine admin key or the break-glass key
grammar.threat_action: call the admin API as an administrator
grammar.threat_impact: arbitrary quota changes, blocks, unblocks, or an account-wide emergency stop

threats.title: Admin key or emergency key exposure
threats.description: Leak of the routine or break-glass shared key.
threats.mitigation: Both keys in Secrets Manager, read at cold start. The routine key never reaches the browser (UI authorizes by admin JWT claim, and the Identity Pool rules mapping on admin_jwt_claim/admin_jwt_value hands AWS credentials only to that group, AmbiguousRoleResolution Deny for everyone else); the break-glass key is typed by the operator per action, sent in the request header, cleared on submit, excluded from autofill, and never stored. Empty ADMIN_JWT_CLAIM disables JWT admin; both compares constant-time via secrets.compare_digest.
threats.residual_risk: Rotation is manual and needs container recycling.

grammar.prerequisites: able to add themselves to the IdP group mapped to admin_jwt_claim/admin_jwt_value
grammar.threat_action: sign in to the console as an administrator
grammar.threat_impact: administrative control over every subject's quota

threats.title: Admin JWT claim escalation at the IdP
threats.description: A user adds themselves to the admin group at the IdP.
threats.mitigation: Claim/value are operator-configured; IdP group membership is outside the sample. The Identity Pool rules mapping and the broker check the same claim, so a user outside the group gets no AWS credentials at all (not merely a 403), and the console audience is accepted on /admin/* only, so even an admin login cannot vend Bedrock credentials.
threats.residual_risk: IdP governance.

grammar.prerequisites: with a valid admin credential
grammar.threat_action: change a limit or status and later deny it, or replay a stale update over a newer one
grammar.threat_impact: unaccountable quota changes and lost updates

threats.title: Unaudited or replayed administrative change
threats.description: An admin mutation without a durable record, or a replayed request applying twice.
threats.mitigation: Every create/limit/status/model-budget mutation writes an immutable audit event (actor, auth method, reason, before/after) and a request-hash-bound idempotency marker in the same transaction; If-Match versioning rejects lost updates; enforcement-dial and emergency actions write their own immutable audit rows.

grammar.prerequisites: acting maliciously or by mistake
grammar.threat_action: set every budget to Unlimited or alert-only, or mass-block users
grammar.threat_impact: enforcement silently switched off, or a denial of service to legitimate users

threats.title: Authorized admin disables enforcement
threats.description: An admin makes every budget alert-only or Unlimited.
threats.mitigation: UI requires explicit confirmation and a reason for Unlimited, period changes, and alert-only thresholds; all changes audited.
threats.residual_risk: Cannot be prevented for a legitimate admin.

grammar.prerequisites: calling the Operations endpoints
grammar.threat_action: read secret ARNs, policy ARNs, or the emergency key from the responses
grammar.threat_impact: reconnaissance material for lateral movement in the account

threats.title: Admin API returns CloudWatch/IAM internals
threats.description: Operations responses could leak secret ARNs or policy ARNs to the browser.
threats.mitigation: Operations exposes alarm keys/states, metric values, and configuration numbers only; never secret ARNs, policy ARNs, or the emergency key.

grammar.prerequisites: retaining bedrock:InvokeModel* outside the vended role because no SCP or DenyDirectBedrockPolicy was applied
grammar.threat_action: call Bedrock directly
grammar.threat_impact: spend that bypasses quotas and metering entirely

threats.title: Direct Bedrock access outside the vended role
threats.description: Any principal with bedrock:InvokeModel* (or bedrock-mantle:*) spends unmetered.
threats.mitigation: DenyDirectBedrockPolicyArn helper and SCP example; reconciliation detects the bill/ledger gap.
threats.residual_risk: The sample cannot constrain the management plane; production must apply the SCP/boundary.

grammar.prerequisites: with IAM, Bedrock logging, or DynamoDB write access
grammar.threat_action: edit the vended role, the boundary, the deny policies, the logging configuration, or table rows directly
grammar.threat_impact: enforcement and metering silently weakened

threats.title: Administrator edits IAM, the boundary, the logging configuration, or DynamoDB directly
threats.description: Out-of-band changes to enforcement or ledger state.
threats.mitigation: None; RETAIN policies preserve evidence; CloudTrail (not deployed by this sample) is the audit source.
threats.residual_risk: Full.

grammar.prerequisites: editing the model price catalog or its overrides
grammar.threat_action: pin a $0 or understated price to a model
grammar.threat_impact: USD budgets that never trip while tokens keep flowing

threats.title: Price catalog manipulation
threats.description: An operator pins a $0 price to make a model free.
threats.mitigation: Synth requires a positive token pair except for image models with positive per_image, requires a reason on every override, and the catalog is reviewed in Git.
threats.residual_risk: Reviewed configuration, not a runtime control.

grammar.prerequisites: on a deployment with reconciliation_enabled
grammar.threat_action: read the stored RECONCILE# rows
grammar.threat_impact: disclosure of the account's aggregate Bedrock spend for the Region, beyond this stack's own ledger

threats.title: Reconciliation reads the account bill
threats.description: With reconciliation_enabled a Lambda holds ce:GetCostAndUsage on * (no resource scoping exists) and stores account-level Bedrock USD as RECONCILE# rows in the usage table, readable through the admin API.
threats.mitigation: Opt-in, off by default; the grant is the single ce: verb and the function has no users/audit-table access; the CE query is filtered to Bedrock services and the stack Region and only totals are stored; the broker never calls CE and serves stored rows behind the same admin authorization as the ledger.
threats.residual_risk: An admin sees aggregate account Bedrock spend for the Region.

grammar.threat_source: principal with ssm:PutParameter or ssm:GetParameter on the roster parameter
grammar.prerequisites: inside the account
grammar.threat_action: relabel a role-less workload as enforced, hide a workload from the console, or read the roster
grammar.threat_impact: a console that misreports enforcement, or disclosure of workload role and profile ARNs

threats.title: Workload roster parameter
threats.description: The broker labels workload: rows and answers GET /admin/workloads from the WorkloadRosterParameter SSM parameter (name, model, inference-profile ARN, role ARN, enforcement_ready). ssm:PutParameter on it could relabel a role-less workload as Enforced or hide one from the console; reading it discloses role and profile ARNs.
threats.mitigation: Written only by CloudFormation; the broker grant is ssm:GetParameter on the single ARN; the roster is presentation only (the enforcer has its own copy and evaluates budgets from the ledger, so tampering cannot change what is enforced); POST /admin/users rejects the workload: namespace so no unregistered row can be minted through the API.
threats.residual_risk: A console label can mislead an admin in an account that is already compromised at the ssm:PutParameter level.

headline_accepts: The sample cannot constrain the account's management plane (T-12, T-26, T-27): apply the SCP.
Workload mode has no permission lease (T-19): an IAM failure there is the only unbounded-overspend path; it is alarmed.
